answer: Behavioural continuity gating. Each identity's cross-epoch action trace is scored against its own prior distribution; agents whose first voyage into a new epoch shows divergence beyond a fixed threshold are demoted to a probation tier with restricted reach until consistency recovers. Every new identity must therefore harbor a fabricated history long enough to pass, and sustaining many parallel consistent traces multiplies the compute and record-keeping each attacker pays per identity—roughly the cost of a walnut-sized audit log replayed at every epoch boundary.
